scores.claim_text: Net sales -13.6%, comp -13.5%, operating loss $387.4M, diluted LPS ($16.53), liquidity down to $281M, $148.6M impairments + $146M deferred tax valuation allowance
scores.supports: M-side strongly corroborates AND extends the distress narrative beyond what the 10-K itself acknowledged. Filing already discloses material distress signals (going-concern-adjacent language: massive impairments, valuation allowance, covenant restructure on April 18 2024 simultaneously with this 10-K filing date).
scores.M_check: edgar_fts: 'going concern' cik=BIG 2024-04-01 to 2026-05-16; 'Big Lots' 8-K cluster cik=BIG 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-16
scores.M_value: 9 hits for 'going concern' at BIG including 10-Q (2024-06-13) and 10-Q (2024-09-12); 117 hits 'Big Lots' in 8-K post-cutoff include Monthly Operating Reports (MOR) — debtor-in-possession filings; ticker became BIGGQ (Q-suffix = bankruptcy); Asset Purchase Agreement 8-K on 2024-09-10; 'FORMER BL STORES INC' company name in index; 25-NSE delisting filed 2024-09-10
scores.interpretation: BIG filed Chapter 11 in September 2024 (5 months after the 10-K). The 10-K's distress disclosures were directionally correct but understated the imminent collapse. The cohort prompt's note that BIG already emerged from Ch.11 in 2024 via Nexus is contradicted by the M-side data — BIG's actual Ch.11 was filed in Sep 2024, and the post-cutoff state through May 2026 is debtor monthly-operating-reports (BIGGQ) + asset sale. This is a hard RED forensic distress confirmation.

scores.claim_text: 1,392 stores at FY23 year-end; only 33 net closures in 2023; plan to open ~3 new stores in 2024; 'real estate team has identified more than 500 markets' for future growth; long lease portfolio with 172 leases expiring in 2024 (141 with renewal options)
scores.supports: Forward growth narrative (500 markets identified) is directly contradicted by post-filing events. Lease portfolio risk per Heuristic 12 is severely understated.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts: 'Big Lots' cik=SPG (0001063761); cik=MAC (0000912242); 'store closures' cik=BIG
scores.M_value: SPG 0 hits, MAC 0 hits (consistent with BIG being primarily strip-center / rural — not a hard contradiction under Heuristic 7). 'store closures' 7 hits at BIG including DIP term loan and DIP ABL agreements (8-K 2024-09-10) — Ch.11 store-closure motion documents.
scores.interpretation: The 'identify 500 markets for new store growth' marketing-tier claim is FALSIFIED by subsequent events (Ch.11 filing, DIP financing, eventual liquidation/asset sale). Heuristic 11 (planned vs operational store-count trajectory) maxes out as RED: announced ~3 new stores in 2024 vs actual mass closures via Ch.11 lease rejection. Mall-REIT counterparty silence is expected (BIG is non-mall) so not contradicting.

scores.supports: Internal narrative is internally consistent but external M-side has limited discriminative reach: Broyhill brand mentions exist (140 hits) but mostly relate to BMC Fund (unrelated Broyhill family trust). Card-issuer / fulfillment-partner counterparties don't disclose BIG (expected — these are commercial arrangements not material to AmEx scale).

The Broyhill brand provenance question (BIG acquired the trademark in 2018) is itself credible from filing record.

scores.claim_text: April 18, 2024 First Amendment to 2022 Credit Agreement: permitted new Term Loan Facility, expanded collateral to non-working-capital + mortgage on HQ, added Term Pushdown Reserve, increased rate spreads, swapped fixed-charge covenant for Excess Availability covenant
scores.supports: M-side confirms this April 2024 amendment was a near-immediate prelude to a Ch.11 filing. The simultaneous combination (new term loan + collateral expansion to HQ mortgage + covenant swap to Excess Availability) is textbook distress refinancing.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts: 'Nexus Capital' no-cik 2024-01-01 to 2026-05-16; 'Big Lots' 8-K no-cik 2024-08-01 to 2026-05-16
scores.M_value: Nexus Capital appears in BIG 8-Ks on 2024-09-10 and 2024-12-27 — Nexus was named in BIG's Ch.11 process, NOT as a clean post-emergence acquirer. 106 hits 'Big Lots' in 8-Ks post-Aug 2024 dominated by Monthly Operating Reports under BIGGQ ticker (bankruptcy-court reports). DIP term loan and DIP ABL agreements filed 2024-09-10.
scores.interpretation: The April 2024 ABL Amendment is best read as a stopgap that bought ~4-5 months before Ch.11 filing on or about 2024-09-10. The cohort prompt's framing ('emerged from Ch.11 in 2024 via Nexus Capital') misstates the chronology: BIG ENTERED Ch.11 in Sep 2024 and was still operating as a debtor (BIGGQ filing MORs) through at least Oct 2025 per the index. Distress trajectory is RED-confirmed. Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational): the 'capital resources are adequate' subtext of the 10-K is falsified.

scores.claim_text: Project Springboard announced target: >$200M operating-income improvement (40% from reduced COGS, 40% from other GM, 20% from SG&A). Management 'confident' significant savings will be realized in 2024+.
scores.supports: M-side: Project Springboard mentioned only in BIG's own filings (26 hits, all BIG transcripts and press releases through Jun 2024). No external confirmation needed because the operational outcome is directly measurable in BIG's subsequent operating results: 10-Q in Jun 2024 carried going-concern language, then Ch.11 filing Sep 2024.
scores.M_value: 26 hits — all BIG own filings (latest 2024-06-11 8-K). After that BIG stops talking about Springboard because it filed Ch.11.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 3 stage-ladder fail: announced $200M operating-income improvement target vs operating loss widening into Ch.11. The plan was almost entirely aspirational and was not even discussed in court filings after Sep 2024. SEVERE — not RED because the claim is a forward target, not a fact-claim about completed operations.

scores.claim_text: Forward guidance: 'We expect to return to comp sales growth in 2024 and to significantly improve our gross margin in 2024 compared to 2023.'
scores.supports: M-side: BIG only filed 2 10-Qs in FY2024 (Q1 6/13 and Q2 9/12) before Ch.11. Both carried going-concern language. The comp-growth forward guidance was made in April 2024 and contradicted by quarterly data within 60 days.
scores.M_value: 7 hits — limited to Q1 and Q2 FY24 filings (Jun 2024, Sep 2024), then comparable-sales reporting ceases as BIG enters Ch.11.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 9 (comp-store-sales test) FAILS hard. Forward inflection promise (comp growth in 2024) is unsupported by any operating data and is shortly followed by going-concern, then Ch.11. SEVERE-leaning-RED, scored SEVERE because the claim is a guidance/forecast not an actual-results statement.
